At compile time, checked word for word by the message tests of `test/messages` with clang:

[cols="2,1,7",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Checked on |The message, and its fix

|`+aead_not_a_family+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: ciphers::basic_chacha20_poly1305 takes an AEAD family: families::chacha20_poly1305, families::chacha20_poly1305_original or families::xchacha20_poly1305.+`

The fix: Name one of the three ChaCha20-Poly1305 families; AES-GCM is `+ciphers::gcm+`, as in `+aes256_gcm+`, and a secret box `+secret_key_encryption::basic_secretbox+`, as in `+secret_key_encryption::secretbox<>+`.

|`+aead_template_removed+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+no member named 'aead' in namespace 'webcpp::crypto::ciphers'+`

The fix: Name `+ciphers::basic_chacha20_poly1305<Family, Backend>+`, or its aliases `+chacha20_poly1305+`, `+chacha20_poly1305_original+` and `+xchacha20_poly1305+`: the template is named for its algorithm, with no alias.

|`+aead_template_removed_call+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+no template named 'aead' in namespace 'webcpp::crypto::ciphers'+`

The fix: As `+aead_template_removed+`: name `+ciphers::basic_chacha20_poly1305+`.

|`+aes_block_default_not_linked+`
|native
|`+webcpp::crypto: AES block cipher's default backend on this target is OpenSSL, which is not linked. Add /webcpp/crypto//aes_block-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//aes_block-default ; or name another backend in the type, as in ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes>. The backends that have it: openssl (native, wasip2, wasip3), ctaes (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten). (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_OPENSSL=1 and link libcrypto)+`

The fix: Natively the block cipher's default is OpenSSL: add `+/webcpp/crypto//aes_block-default+`, which links `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` there, or name ctaes in the type, as in `+aes256<backends::ctaes>+`.

|`+aes_block_default_not_linked_wasm+`
|wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: AES block cipher's default backend on this target is ctaes, which is not linked. Add /webcpp/crypto//aes_block-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//aes_block-default ; or name another backend in the type, as in ciphers::aes256<backends::openssl>. The backends that have it: openssl (native, wasip2, wasip3), ctaes (native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten). (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_CTAES=1 and link ctaes.c with webcpp's src/canary_ctaes.c)+`

The fix: On WASI the block cipher's default is ctaes: add `+/webcpp/crypto//aes_block-default+`, which links `+/third_party//ctaes+` there, or, with OpenSSL linked, name it in the type, as in `+aes256<backends::openssl>+`.

|`+aes_on_bearssl+`
|native, wasip2
|`+webcpp::crypto: ciphers::aes256<backends::bearssl>: BearSSL exports AES only inside its modes, with no block cipher. Name a backend that exports it, as in ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes> or ciphers::aes256<backends::openssl>, and add its library to the program's Jamfile.+`

The fix: Name `+ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes>+`, include `+<webcpp/crypto/backends/ctaes.hpp>+` and add `+/third_party//ctaes+`.

|`+agree_asynchronous_backend+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: agree on this backend completes asynchronously: call async_agree.+`

The fix: Call `+async_agree+` on a backend that completes by itself: its synchronous forms cannot wait for it.

|`+agree_ed25519+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: agree: Ed25519 key pairs sign; they do not agree: convert one with to_x25519() and agree with the X25519 key pair.+`

The fix: Convert the Ed25519 key pair with `+to_x25519()+` and agree with the X25519 key pair it gives, and the peer's key converted with `+public_key.to_x25519()+`: an Ed25519 key pair signs and does not agree.

|`+agree_free_wrong_peer+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: agree: this key pair does not agree with this peer: an X25519 key pair agrees with a curves::x25519::public_key, a P-256 key pair with a curves::p256::basic_public_key of its backend, a secp256k1 key pair with a curves::secp256k1::public_key.+`

The fix: Give `+agree+` the peer's typed public key of the key pair's own curve and backend: `+curves::x25519::public_key::from_bytes(bytes)+` for X25519, `+curves::p256::basic_public_key<Backend>::from_bytes(bytes)+` for P-256, `+curves::secp256k1::public_key::from_bytes(bytes)+` for secp256k1.

|`+async_agree_ed25519+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_agree: Ed25519 key pairs sign; they do not agree: convert one with to_x25519() and agree with the X25519 key pair.+`

The fix: As `+agree_ed25519+`: give `+async_agree+` the X25519 key pair that the Ed25519 key pair's `+to_x25519()+` gives, and the peer's converted key.

|`+async_agree_secp256k1+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_agree takes a key pair of an algorithm WebCrypto has (X25519, P-256): call the key pair's synchronous agree for the others.+`

The fix: Call the key pair's own `+agree+`: secp256k1 is not in WebCrypto, so only X25519's and P-256's key pairs have `+async_agree+`.

|`+async_agree_wrong_peer+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_agree: this key pair does not agree with this peer: an X25519 key pair agrees with a curves::x25519::public_key, a P-256 key pair with a curves::p256::basic_public_key of its backend.+`

The fix: As `+agree_free_wrong_peer+`: give `+async_agree+` the peer's typed public key of the key pair's own curve and backend, `+curves::x25519::public_key::from_bytes(bytes)+` for X25519, `+curves::p256::basic_public_key<Backend>::from_bytes(bytes)+` for P-256.

|`+async_from_key_secretbox_asynchronous_backend+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WebCrypto has no ChaCha20-Poly1305, XChaCha20-Poly1305, secret box or crypto_box: no form of them, synchronous or asynchronous, runs on the browser's backend; name a native backend for them. On the browser's backend only AES-GCM seals and opens.+`

The fix: Name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for the secret box's `+async_from_key+`: WebCrypto has no secret box.

|`+async_from_key_xchacha+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WebCrypto has no ChaCha20-Poly1305, XChaCha20-Poly1305, secret box or crypto_box: no form of them, synchronous or asynchronous, runs on the browser's backend; name a native backend for them. On the browser's backend only AES-GCM seals and opens.+`

The fix: Name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for `+async_from_key+`: WebCrypto has no XChaCha20-Poly1305, so no form of it runs on the browser's backend, where only AES-GCM seals and opens.

|`+async_from_secret_secp256k1+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_from_secret takes a key pair of an algorithm WebCrypto has (Ed25519, X25519, P-256): call the synchronous from_secret for the others.+`

The fix: Call the synchronous `+from_secret+`: secp256k1 is not in WebCrypto, so only Ed25519's, X25519's and P-256's key pairs have `+async_from_secret+`.

|`+async_member_without_async_hpp+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+with deduced return type cannot be used before it is defined+`

The fix: Include `+<webcpp/crypto/async.hpp>+`, which defines the asynchronous members, and add `+<library>/webcpp/asio//asio+` to the program's Jamfile.

|`+async_open_box_asynchronous_backend+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WebCrypto has no ChaCha20-Poly1305, XChaCha20-Poly1305, secret box or crypto_box: no form of them, synchronous or asynchronous, runs on the browser's backend; name a native backend for them. On the browser's backend only AES-GCM seals and opens.+`

The fix: Name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for the crypto_box: WebCrypto has no crypto_box, so no form of it runs on the browser's backend, where only AES-GCM seals and opens.

|`+async_open_xchacha+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WebCrypto has no ChaCha20-Poly1305, XChaCha20-Poly1305, secret box or crypto_box: no form of them, synchronous or asynchronous, runs on the browser's backend; name a native backend for them. On the browser's backend only AES-GCM seals and opens.+`

The fix: Name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for `+async_open+`, or open with AES-GCM on the browser's backend: WebCrypto has no XChaCha20-Poly1305.

|`+async_seal_box_associated_data+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_seal: a secret box or a crypto_box takes no associated data: secret_key_encryption::async_seal(executor, box, nonce, data, token).+`

The fix: Call the box form, `+secret_key_encryption::async_seal(executor, box, nonce, data, token)+`, or the box's own `+async_seal(executor, nonce, data, token)+`: a secret box or a crypto_box takes no associated data.

|`+async_seal_box_asynchronous_backend+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WebCrypto has no ChaCha20-Poly1305, XChaCha20-Poly1305, secret box or crypto_box: no form of them, synchronous or asynchronous, runs on the browser's backend; name a native backend for them. On the browser's backend only AES-GCM seals and opens.+`

The fix: Name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for the secret box: WebCrypto has no secret box, so no form of it runs on the browser's backend, where only AES-GCM seals and opens.

|`+async_seal_member_asynchronous_backend+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WebCrypto has no ChaCha20-Poly1305, XChaCha20-Poly1305, secret box or crypto_box: no form of them, synchronous or asynchronous, runs on the browser's backend; name a native backend for them. On the browser's backend only AES-GCM seals and opens.+`

The fix: As `+async_seal_xchacha+`: name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for XChaCha20-Poly1305's `+async_seal+`.

|`+async_seal_removed+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+no member named 'async_seal' in namespace 'webcpp::crypto'; did you mean 'webcpp::crypto::secret_key_encryption::async_seal'?+`

`+no member named 'async_open' in namespace 'webcpp::crypto'; did you mean 'webcpp::crypto::secret_key_encryption::async_open'?+`

The fix: Call crypto::secret_key_encryption::aead::async_seal and async_open. clang's suggestion, `+secret_key_encryption::async_seal+` and `+async_open+`, is the box form, which takes no associated data and is wrong for an AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 user.

|`+async_seal_removed_declaration+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+no member named 'async_seal' in namespace 'webcpp::crypto'+`

`+no member named 'async_open' in namespace 'webcpp::crypto'+`

The fix: As `+async_seal_removed+`: call crypto::secret_key_encryption::aead::async_seal and async_open, in <webcpp/crypto/async.hpp>.

|`+async_seal_xchacha+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WebCrypto has no ChaCha20-Poly1305, XChaCha20-Poly1305, secret box or crypto_box: no form of them, synchronous or asynchronous, runs on the browser's backend; name a native backend for them. On the browser's backend only AES-GCM seals and opens.+`

The fix: Name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for `+async_seal+`, or seal with AES-GCM on the browser's backend: WebCrypto has no XChaCha20-Poly1305.

|`+async_sign_ed25519_prehashed+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: crypto::eddsa signs the message itself (RFC 8032's pure Ed25519) and takes no digest; a message's SHA-512 is signed with crypto::eddsa_prehashed (Ed25519ph).+`

The fix: Give `+async_sign+` the message itself with `+crypto::eddsa+`, RFC 8032's pure Ed25519, which takes no digest, as the synchronous `+sign+` does; a message's SHA-512 is signed with `+crypto::eddsa_prehashed+` (Ed25519ph), on a native backend.

|`+async_sign_eddsa_prehashed_asynchronous_backend+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WebCrypto has no Ed25519ph: crypto::eddsa_prehashed's sign, verify, async_sign and async_verify run on a native backend.+`

The fix: As `+sign_eddsa_prehashed_asynchronous_backend+`: `+async_sign+` under `+crypto::eddsa_prehashed+` runs on a native backend.

|`+async_sign_p256_eddsa+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_sign: this key pair does not sign with this scheme: an Ed25519 key pair signs with crypto::eddsa or crypto::eddsa_prehashed, a P-256 key pair with crypto::ecdsa_sha256.+`

The fix: Give `+async_sign+` the key pair's own scheme: `+crypto::ecdsa_sha256+` for a P-256 key pair, `+crypto::eddsa+` or `+crypto::eddsa_prehashed+` for an Ed25519 key pair.

|`+async_sign_secp256k1+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_sign takes a key pair of an algorithm WebCrypto has (Ed25519, P-256): call the key pair's synchronous signing function for the others.+`

The fix: Call the key pair's own signing function: secp256k1 is not in WebCrypto, so only Ed25519's and P-256's key pairs have `+async_sign+`.

|`+async_sign_x25519+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_sign: X25519 key pairs agree; they do not sign: sign with an Ed25519 key pair, which to_x25519() converts for agreement.+`

The fix: As `+sign_x25519+`: give `+async_sign+` an Ed25519 key pair, which signs; an X25519 key pair agrees, with `+async_agree+`.

|`+async_verify_eddsa_bytes_key+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_verify takes crypto::eddsa or crypto::eddsa_prehashed with a curves::ed25519::public_key or crypto::ecdsa_sha256 with a curves::p256::basic_public_key, the algorithms WebCrypto has: call crypto::verify for the others.+`

The fix: Give `+async_verify+` with `+crypto::eddsa+` the public key as a `+curves::ed25519::public_key+`, as `+crypto::verify+` takes it: `+key_pair.public_key()+`, or `+curves::ed25519::public_key::from_bytes(bytes)+`.

|`+async_verify_eddsa_prehashed_asynchronous_backend+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: WebCrypto has no Ed25519ph: crypto::eddsa_prehashed's sign, verify, async_sign and async_verify run on a native backend.+`

The fix: As `+verify_eddsa_prehashed_asynchronous_backend+`: `+async_verify+` under `+crypto::eddsa_prehashed+`, free and member, runs on a native backend.

|`+async_verify_named_backend+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_verify takes crypto::eddsa or crypto::eddsa_prehashed with a curves::ed25519::public_key or crypto::ecdsa_sha256 with a curves::p256::basic_public_key, the algorithms WebCrypto has: call crypto::verify for the others.+`

The fix: As `+async_verify_wrong_key+`: naming the backend does not add a scheme; call `+crypto::verify+` for `+crypto::schnorr+` and secp256k1's keys.

|`+async_verify_p256_bytes_signature+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: verify: a P-256 key verifies a curves::p256::ecdsa_signature: make one from 64 bytes with curves::p256::ecdsa_signature::from_bytes.+`

The fix: As `+verify_p256_secp256k1_signature+`: make the 64 bytes received into a `+curves::p256::ecdsa_signature+` with `+from_bytes+`, then give it to `+async_verify+`.

|`+async_verify_wrong_key+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: async_verify takes crypto::eddsa or crypto::eddsa_prehashed with a curves::ed25519::public_key or crypto::ecdsa_sha256 with a curves::p256::basic_public_key, the algorithms WebCrypto has: call crypto::verify for the others.+`

The fix: Call `+crypto::verify+` for a key the asynchronous family lacks (secp256k1's, Schnorr's x-only key): `+async_verify+` has a `+curves::ed25519::public_key+` with `+crypto::eddsa+` or `+crypto::eddsa_prehashed+` and a `+curves::p256::basic_public_key+` with `+crypto::ecdsa_sha256+`.

|`+erase_secret_const_range+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
|`+webcpp::crypto: erase_secret zeroes a buffer the program may write, of trivially copyable elements: a std::vector<std::uint8_t>, a std::string, a std::array, a std::span<std::byte>; this range's elements are const or not trivially copyable.+`

The fix: Erase the buffer the secret was written to, through a non-const reference to it (`+std::string&+`, `+std::span<std::byte>+`): a const view cannot be erased. Its elements must be trivially copyable, bytes or integers; a range of `+std::string+` or of another type with its own storage cannot be erased as bytes, so erase each element's buffer instead.

The fix: Remove `+<define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE+` from the WebAssembly build: give that build a project of its own, without the define and OpenSSL, naming `+/third_party//bearssl+`. On WebAssembly the backend is BearSSL, which allocates nothing.
+
Its Jamfile:
+
[listing]
----
include::{webcpp-root}/tools/test/fixtures/crypto_jamfiles/openssl_memory_on_emscripten/Jamfile[tag=jamfile]
----
+
On each target, the build's output contains:
+
* emscripten:
** `+webcpp::crypto: WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE is an option of native programs, and this program is built for WebAssembly. Remove that define from the program's Jamfile.+`

`+openssl_on_emscripten+`:: `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` named in a build for Emscripten. The fix: Name `+/third_party//bearssl+` in its place for the Emscripten build.

On each target, the build's output contains:

** `+webcpp::crypto: /webcpp/crypto//openssl is named in a build for Emscripten, where webcpp does not build OpenSSL.+`

Add /webcpp/crypto//p256-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//p256-default ; (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_BEARSSL=1 and link BearSSL built with webcpp's src/canary_bearssl.c)+`

`+p256_on_sodium_on_emscripten+`:: A program for Emscripten that names libsodium, which has no P-256, in a P-256 key pair's type. The fix: As `+p256_on_sodium+`.

`+pem_default_not_linked_on_emscripten+`:: A program for Emscripten that armours DER as PEM on its default, libsodium, and links none. The fix: As `+pem_default_not_linked+`.

Add /webcpp/crypto//x25519-default, the default's library on every target, to the program's Jamfile, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//x25519-default ; (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_SODIUM=1 and link libsodium built with webcpp's src/canary_sodium.c)+`

On MSVC, each case of `test/msvc` is proven to stop the build, at compile or at link time; its text is MSVC's own, the same instruction in MSVC's words, and two files compiled with different settings stop the link with LNK2038.

[cols="1,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Stops |Fix

|`+aead_not_a_family+`
|the compile
|Name one of the three ChaCha20-Poly1305 families; AES-GCM is `+ciphers::gcm+`, as in `+aes256_gcm+`, and a secret box `+secret_key_encryption::basic_secretbox+`, as in `+secret_key_encryption::secretbox<>+`.

|`+aes_block_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Natively the block cipher's default is OpenSSL: add `+/webcpp/crypto//aes_block-default+`, which links `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` there, or name ctaes in the type, as in `+aes256<backends::ctaes>+`.

|`+aes_on_bearssl+`
|the compile
|Name `+ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes>+`, include `+<webcpp/crypto/backends/ctaes.hpp>+` and add `+/third_party//ctaes+`.

|`+async_from_key_xchacha+`
|the compile
|Name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for `+async_from_key+`: WebCrypto has no XChaCha20-Poly1305, so no form of it runs on the browser's backend, where only AES-GCM seals and opens.

|`+async_from_secret_secp256k1+`
|the compile
|Call the synchronous `+from_secret+`: secp256k1 is not in WebCrypto, so only Ed25519's, X25519's and P-256's key pairs have `+async_from_secret+`.

|`+async_open_xchacha+`
|the compile
|Name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for `+async_open+`, or open with AES-GCM on the browser's backend: WebCrypto has no XChaCha20-Poly1305.

|`+async_seal_xchacha+`
|the compile
|Name a native backend, such as `+backends::sodium+`, for `+async_seal+`, or seal with AES-GCM on the browser's backend: WebCrypto has no XChaCha20-Poly1305.

|`+async_sign_secp256k1+`
|the compile
|Call the key pair's own signing function: secp256k1 is not in WebCrypto, so only Ed25519's and P-256's key pairs have `+async_sign+`.

|`+bearssl_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/third_party//bearssl+`.

|`+box_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|The secret boxes', the boxes' and the sealed boxes' default is libsodium on every target: add the family's alias, as `+/webcpp/crypto//box_xsalsa20poly1305-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+box_not_a_family+`
|the compile
|Name `+families::box_xsalsa20poly1305+` or `+families::box_xchacha20poly1305+`, or use `+public_key_encryption::box+` or `+public_key_encryption::box_xchacha20poly1305+`.

|`+canary_ctaes_missing+`
|the link
|Link `+/third_party//ctaes+`.

|`+canary_missing+`
|the link
|Link the library through b2, `+/third_party//bearssl+`; built by other means, it must be the pinned commit, with webcpp's `+src/canary_bearssl.c+`.

|`+canary_other_commit+`
|the link
|Build the library at the commit of webcpp's submodule, or link it through b2.

|`+canary_other_configuration+`
|the link
|Build BearSSL in webcpp's configuration (`+getentropy+`), or link it through b2.

|`+canary_secp256k1_missing+`
|the link
|Link `+/third_party//secp256k1+`.

|`+canary_secp256k1_small+`
|the link
|Give the program and the library the same `+<webcpp-secp256k1-tables>+`, or link through b2.

|`+canary_secp256k1_two_files+`
|the link
|Compile every file of the program with the same backend settings.

|`+canary_sodium_other_commit+`
|the link
|Build the library at the commit of webcpp's submodule, or link it through b2.

|`+canary_two_files+`
|the link
|Compile every file of the program with the same backend settings.

|`+chacha_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|The ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs' default is libsodium on every target: add the family's alias, as `+/webcpp/crypto//chacha20_poly1305-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+chacha_header_not_included+`
|the compile
|Include the backend's header the message names, as `+<webcpp/crypto/backends/bearssl.hpp>+`, and add its library, as `+/third_party//bearssl+`.

|`+chacha_on_ctaes+`
|the compile
|Name a backend that has ChaCha20-Poly1305, as in `+chacha20_poly1305<backends::bearssl>+`, or its default, `+chacha20_poly1305<>+`, and link its library.

|`+chacha_unknown_backend+`
|the compile
|Name a backend of `+webcpp::crypto::backends+` that has the family, as `+backends::bearssl+`, or leave the backend out for the family's default: `+chacha20_poly1305<>+`.

|`+ctaes_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/third_party//ctaes+`.

|`+default_openssl_wasm+`
|the compile
|Remove the define, and name `+gcm<aes256<backends::openssl>>+` where the program wants OpenSSL.

|`+default_selected+`
|the compile
|Remove the define, and name `+gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>+` where the program wants BearSSL.

|`+ed25519_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//ed25519-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.

|`+ed25519_on_bearssl+`
|the compile
|Leave the backend out, as in `+curves::ed25519::keypair+`, or name `+backends::sodium+`, and add `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+ed25519_unknown_policy+`
|the compile
|Leave the policy out, as in `+crypto::verify(crypto::eddsa, signature, message, public_key)+`, or name `+curves::ed25519::strict+`.

|`+ed25519ph_sha256+`
|the compile
|Name `+curves::ed25519::prehashed_signer<webcpp::hash::sha2_512>+`: RFC 8032 defines Ed25519ph over SHA-512.

|`+ellswift_other_backend+`
|the compile
|Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::ellswift_decode(encoded_key)+`.

|`+gcm_default_openssl_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Natively the default is OpenSSL: add `+/webcpp/crypto//gcm-default+`, which links `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` there, or name BearSSL in the type, as in `+gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>+`.

|`+gcm_on_ctaes+`
|the compile
|Name `+gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>+` or `+gcm<aes256<backends::openssl>>+`, or use `+aes256_gcm+` with its default linked.

|`+heavy_without_threads+`
|the compile
|Call the synchronous operation the message names, or build with threads: natively without `+WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_THREADS+`, on Emscripten with `+-pthread+`; WASI has none.

|`+kx_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//kx-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.

|`+label_lookup_by_value+`
|the compile
|Return `+std::optional<std::span<std::uint8_t const, 32>>+`, a span over a tweak the lookup keeps, such as a map's entry; never the tweak by value.

|`+memory_missing_definition_from_key+`
|the link
|Define `+std::pmr::memory_resource& webcpp::crypto::openssl_memory_resource() noexcept+` once in the program, returning a resource that is never destroyed.

|`+memory_missing_definition_install+`
|the link
|Define `+std::pmr::memory_resource& webcpp::crypto::openssl_memory_resource() noexcept+` once in the program, returning a resource that is never destroyed.

|`+memory_two_files+`
|the link
|Give the define in the requirements of the program's project, with OpenSSL beside it, `+project app : requirements <define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE <library>/webcpp/crypto//openssl ;+`, so that every target of the program gets both.

|`+musig_nonce_copied+`
|the compile
|Pass the nonce with std::move, once: a secret nonce signs one message.

|`+musig_other_backend+`
|the compile
|Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::musig::parse_public_nonce(encoded_nonce)+`.

|`+openssl_memory_not_linked+`
|the compile
|A target has the define and not OpenSSL: put `+<library>/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` in the same project requirements as the define, or remove the define.

|`+openssl_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+`.

|`+openssl_old+`
|the compile
|Name `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+`, which builds OpenSSL 3.5.9; without b2, put OpenSSL 3's `+include/+` first.

|`+p256_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//p256-default+`, which links `+/third_party//bearssl+` on every target.

|`+p256_on_sodium+`
|the compile
|Leave the backend out, as in `+curves::p256::keypair+`, or name `+backends::bearssl+`, and add `+/third_party//bearssl+`.

|`+pem_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//pem-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.

|`+secp256k1_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/third_party//secp256k1+`.

|`+secp256k1_other_backend+`
|the compile
|Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::keypair+`.

|`+secret_of_no_bytes+`
|the compile
|Give `+secret+` the number of bytes it holds, at least one, as in `+secret<32>+`.

|`+sign_eddsa_prehashed_message+`
|the compile
|Give `+crypto::eddsa_prehashed+` the message's SHA-512 marked as a digest, `+crypto::prehashed{digest}+` of a `+std::array<std::uint8_t, 64>+`; sign the message itself with `+crypto::eddsa+`, or give it in pieces to `+curves::ed25519::prehashed_signer<webcpp::hash::sha2_512>+`.

|`+sign_keccak_without_xkcp+`
|the compile
|Add `+/third_party//xkcp+` to the program's Jamfile, whose Keccak-256 hashes the message, or build the 32-byte digest elsewhere and sign `+crypto::prehashed{digest}+`, which needs no XKCP.

|`+silent_payments_other_backend+`
|the compile
|Name `+backends::secp256k1+`, or leave the backend out: `+curves::secp256k1::silent_payments::make_previous_outputs_summary(...)+`.

|`+sodium_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/third_party//sodium+`.

|`+x25519_default_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add `+/webcpp/crypto//x25519-default+`, which links `+/third_party//sodium+` on every target.
|===
